The GitHub release body for GeoTools 0.3.0 (and its 0.3.0-* prereleases).
scripts/release_notes.py prints this page with {version} replaced by the
version being released, then a link to the full changelog. Links are absolute
because a release body cannot follow relative links.

GeoTools {version} is the first release of the rebuilt GeoTools: a Blender 5.2
extension that prepares a site in Blender, analyses it, cleans its textures,
and publishes it as OGC 3D Tiles (`.3tz`) with
[rusty-tiles](https://github.com/BenDyson-Arch/rusty-tiles). It also reads
and writes GeoJSON and GeoPackage, and reads GeoTIFF, in the site's
coordinates. It replaces the 0.2 importer add-on: see
[Upgrading from 0.2](#upgrading-from-02) before you install it.

New to GeoTools? [Getting started](https://github.com/BenDyson-Arch/blender_geotools/blob/v{version}/docs/guide/getting-started.md)
takes you from an empty Blender to a published, georeferenced site in about
ten minutes, on synthetic demo data.

## Download

Download the zip for your platform. Each one holds everything GeoTools needs
(rusty-tiles, pyproj with PROJ, and certifi); there is nothing to install with
pip.

| Platform | File |
|---|---|
| Linux x64 | [`geotools-{version}-linux_x64.zip`](https://github.com/BenDyson-Arch/blender_geotools/releases/download/v{version}/geotools-{version}-linux_x64.zip) |
| Windows x64 | [`geotools-{version}-windows_x64.zip`](https://github.com/BenDyson-Arch/blender_geotools/releases/download/v{version}/geotools-{version}-windows_x64.zip) |
| macOS, Apple silicon | [`geotools-{version}-macos_arm64.zip`](https://github.com/BenDyson-Arch/blender_geotools/releases/download/v{version}/geotools-{version}-macos_arm64.zip) |
| Demo data (any platform) | [`geotools-demo-data-{version}.zip`](https://github.com/BenDyson-Arch/blender_geotools/releases/download/v{version}/geotools-demo-data-{version}.zip): the synthetic site used in Getting started |

**Do not install "Source code (zip)" or "Source code (tar.gz)".** GitHub adds
them to every release. They are the repository's source, without the bundled
libraries, and Blender cannot install them as an extension.

### Requirements

- Blender 5.2, an official build from
  [blender.org](https://www.blender.org/download/) (CPython 3.13). A Blender
  built by a Linux distribution against another Python, such as 3.14, refuses
  the zip.
- Linux x64, Windows x64, or macOS 15 or later on Apple silicon. There is no
  build for Intel Macs or Linux arm64.

### Install

1. In Blender, open **Edit > Preferences > Get Extensions**.
2. Open the menu at the top right and choose **Install from Disk...**, then
   pick the zip. Or drag the zip into the Blender window.
3. In the 3D Viewport, press **N** and select the **GeoTools** tab.
4. Open the **About** panel at the bottom of the tab. Its header shows a tick
   when rusty-tiles and pyproj both loaded.

### Check the download

`SHA256SUMS` lists the SHA-256 of every zip in this release. In the folder
that holds the zip and `SHA256SUMS`:

- **Linux:** `sha256sum --ignore-missing -c SHA256SUMS` prints `OK` for each
  zip you downloaded.
- **macOS:** `shasum -a 256 geotools-{version}-macos_arm64.zip`, and compare
  the result with that zip's line in `SHA256SUMS`.
- **Windows (PowerShell):**
  `Get-FileHash geotools-{version}-windows_x64.zip -Algorithm SHA256`, and
  compare the hash with that zip's line in `SHA256SUMS` (PowerShell prints it
  in capitals).

## What is new since 0.2

GeoTools is now an authoring tool for 3D Tiles. Everything is in one sidebar
tab whose panels follow the workflow from top to bottom, and each panel header
shows whether its step is done. Each area has a page in the
[user guide](https://github.com/BenDyson-Arch/blender_geotools/blob/v{version}/docs/guide/README.md).

- **[Georeference and projects](https://github.com/BenDyson-Arch/blender_geotools/blob/v{version}/docs/guide/projects.md):**
  Local, Anchor (a WGS84 point and heading) or CRS projects. The CRS field is
  a searchable EPSG picker over the 3,211 codes rusty-tiles resolves, with the
  datum operation and its accuracy shown before you publish. Offsets keep full
  double precision, offset files are read beside an imported mesh, and
  **Verify Placement** checks where the site lands on Earth.
- **[Working alongside BlenderGIS](https://github.com/BenDyson-Arch/blender_geotools/blob/v{version}/docs/guide/blendergis.md):**
  a CRS project reads and writes the scene's BlenderGIS GeoScene keys, so data
  from either tool lands on the same coordinates. BlenderGIS is not needed.
- **[Checks and publishing](https://github.com/BenDyson-Arch/blender_geotools/blob/v{version}/docs/guide/publish.md):**
  Run Checks against rusty-tiles' input rules, with fix buttons; build
  profiles; publish to a validated `.3tz` in the background, with a build
  record and a face map back to the source.
- **[Layers and bakes](https://github.com/BenDyson-Arch/blender_geotools/blob/v{version}/docs/guide/layers.md):**
  named values per face, corner or texel, read straight from Geometry Nodes
  outputs or stored attributes, texture-space bakes, colour ramps and
  categories, and variant tilesets such as `site.slope.3tz`.
- **[GLB with metadata](https://github.com/BenDyson-Arch/blender_geotools/blob/v{version}/docs/guide/glb-metadata.md):**
  one standard glTF 2.0 file with objects, layers and the georeference as
  `EXT_mesh_features` and `EXT_structural_metadata`.
- **[Analysis](https://github.com/BenDyson-Arch/blender_geotools/blob/v{version}/docs/guide/analysis.md):**
  the sun, sun hours, insolation and shadow studies; archaeoastronomy;
  coordinates, distances and areas on Earth; 3D surface hydrology; contours
  and sections; and a library of Geometry Nodes presets (terrain shape,
  archaeological visualisation, visibility, change and distance, volumes, and
  least-cost paths) that you can open and edit.
- **[Texture cleanup](https://github.com/BenDyson-Arch/blender_geotools/blob/v{version}/docs/guide/textures.md):**
  a one-click paint setup with UV overlaps masked, hole filling, removal of
  masked objects, edge padding and colour balance across texture pages.
- **[Inspecting output](https://github.com/BenDyson-Arch/blender_geotools/blob/v{version}/docs/guide/inspect-output.md):**
  open published tiles in Blender, trace an output triangle to its source
  face and back, and view distance, texel density and level of detail.
- **[Geo formats](https://github.com/BenDyson-Arch/blender_geotools/blob/v{version}/docs/guide/geo-formats.md):**
  GeoJSON and GeoPackage import and export, GeoTIFF import of DEMs and
  orthophotos, linked files that refresh in place, attribute write-back, and
  vector publishing as 3D Tiles. Vector data in another CRS is reprojected
  with the bundled pyproj.

Every change is listed in the [changelog](https://github.com/BenDyson-Arch/blender_geotools/blob/v{version}/CHANGELOG.md).

## Known limitations

The [roadmap](https://github.com/BenDyson-Arch/blender_geotools/blob/v{version}/docs/ROADMAP.md)
says what comes next and why.

- **Some CRSs are refused.** rusty-tiles resolves 3,211 EPSG codes, but not
  grid-based datums (such as British National Grid, EPSG:27700, NAD27 and the
  original NAD83), dynamic frames, compound CRSs with a vertical datum, or
  coordinate epochs. The Project panel says why a CRS is refused.
- **Layer values reach 3D Tiles only as colours**, in variant tilesets.
  Queryable values in the tiles need rusty-tiles 0.5; until then the
  GLB with metadata carries them.
- **Every mesh publish is a full retile.** Changing one layer or texture
  rebuilds the whole archive. Vector publishes update incrementally.
- **Rasters are not reprojected.** Reproject a GeoTIFF in another CRS in QGIS
  first. Rotated or sheared rasters are refused, and GeoTIFF is import only.
- **Large source images.** rusty-tiles refuses images over 16,384 pixels a
  side or with 16 bits per channel. Checks reports them, with a fix that
  changes only the published copy. Below 1 GiB, an image of any encoded size
  publishes if the build's memory budget can hold it.
- **Preview in Browser needs extra software:** a separately installed
  rusty-tiles CLI and a Cesium 1.146 `Build/Cesium` folder, set in the
  preferences. CesiumJS cannot open a `.3tz` directly; extract it and serve
  the folder.
- **Named time zones on Windows.** Blender's Python on Windows usually has no
  time zone database, so the Sun panel takes UTC or a UTC offset there.
- **One Blender session holds the whole site.** There is no chunked mode for
  sources too large for one session yet.

## Upgrading from 0.2

0.3 is a new extension, not an update of the 0.2 add-on. 0.2's importers and
analysis tools are gone; they stay on the
[`legacy-0.2`](https://github.com/BenDyson-Arch/blender_geotools/tree/legacy-0.2)
branch and the [`v0.2.0`](https://github.com/BenDyson-Arch/blender_geotools/releases/tag/v0.2.0)
release.

1. **Remove the 0.2 add-on first.** In **Edit > Preferences > Add-ons**, find
   GeoTools 0.2, untick it and uninstall it. Then install 0.3 as above. The two
   use some of the same operator and panel ids (for example
   `geotools.import_geojson` and the Layers and Analysis panels), so with both
   enabled one of them breaks.
2. **pyproj and GDAL are no longer needed.** 0.2 asked you to install them into
   Blender's Python. 0.3 bundles pyproj and does not use GDAL, so you can
   uninstall them. The About panel names the pyproj that actually loaded.
3. **Blender 5.2 is required** (0.2 ran on 5.1).
4. **Files saved with 0.2** open. 0.2 also wrote the BlenderGIS GeoScene keys
   (`SRID`, `crs x`, `crs y`), and the Project panel offers **Use the Scene's
   BlenderGIS Georeference** to make the project a CRS project from them.
   0.2's own settings (import options, analysis settings, its georeference
   copy) are not read. Objects imported by 0.2 are ordinary meshes; import the
   GeoJSON or GeoPackage again to get a linked file that refreshes.
5. **What replaces 0.2's tools:** GeoTIFF import replaces the DEM importer;
   the Analysis panel and its presets replace slope, aspect, roughness, line
   of sight and shadow; layers read Geometry Nodes outputs directly instead of
   attribute transfer. GeoTools no longer imports 3D Tiles for editing: it
   creates them, and opens its own output only to inspect it.

## Getting help

- The [user guide](https://github.com/BenDyson-Arch/blender_geotools/blob/v{version}/docs/guide/README.md)
  covers each panel, with a limits section per page.
- Report a bug or ask a question in
  [GitHub issues](https://github.com/BenDyson-Arch/blender_geotools/issues).
  Include your platform, the Blender version, and the versions the About panel
  shows (GeoTools, rusty-tiles, pyproj). Please share only data you are free
  to share; a small synthetic file that shows the problem helps most.
